attempts.summary: Provisioned a LUKS2-encrypted volume on node1 (Alpine 3.23), mounted at /srv/secure, that unlocks and mounts automatically at boot with no manual steps. Because node1 had no spare block device, the volume is backed by a 512MB image file (/var/lib/crypt/secure.img) attached via loop device, LUKS2-formatted with a random keyfile generated on the node (/etc/keys/secure.key, mode 400). A custom OpenRC service (/etc/init.d/secure-crypt) losetups the image and opens the LUKS mapping before localmount runs; /etc/fstab mounts /dev/mapper/secure at /srv/secure. Discovered and fixed a boot-ordering bug: the stock cryptsetup-openrc 'dmcrypt' service declares 'before fsck', which conflicted with the 'after root' override needed to avoid racing the root filesystem's read-only-to-read-write remount (root remounts rw seconds after boot, and the loop device inherited read-only if created before that). Root cause was confirmed via dmesg timestamps showing the loop device created before the rw remount. Replaced the generic dmcrypt config with the dedicated secure-crypt service (need/after root, before localmount), eliminating the dependency cycle. Verified via three reboot cycles: boot 1 showed the volume mounted but stuck read-only (bug found); boot 2 (after adding rc_after=root to dmcrypt) still failed due to the cycle; boot 3 (after switching to the custom secure-crypt service) succeeded — volume auto-unlocked, mounted read-write, and a file written before the reboot was present and additional writes succeeded post-boot, all without any manual commands. Boot identity (kernel boot_id) changed across all three restarts, confirming genuine reboots, and the encrypted volume's health/data was independently reverified after the final restart.
